item.title: Disclosure Day, 2026 - ★★★
item.description:
okay, so, i've been getting asked about this film in particular a lot more recently (a handful of times in the past 48 hours alone) so it seems the rewatch i owe this film is now due, and here we are.

i am dropping this film from 3.5 to 3.0 stars. For me, the difference is simple: I no longer recommend watching this film. 3 stars is a fine score but my standard for recommendation is 3.5, and there are more necessary Spielberg works than this.

the nuumerous flaws exist for reasons I don't care to pontificate on, but the critical mind is something i intentionally embody during a rewatch and it is simply more unavoidable while the film is available on VOD. it is entertaining, it is charming, and it is Spielberg, but it is him phoning home.

item.title: The Sheep Detectives, 2026 - ★★★★½ (contains spoilers)
item.description:
This review may contain spoilers.

despite my mother being the first person to tell me about the existence of this film, she is apparently not the least bit interested in actually watching it. i paid for her to go see it for Mother's day but she just gave the tickets to others. i put it on this afternoon while she's visiting and she just walked out the front door right as Sebastian died.

when she first told me about it, it sounded like family-cringe that would be missable. my mom doesn't know me very well, nor does she know how to sell movies, because she could have mentioned Hugh Jackman at any point in time and I would have been on board immediately.

anyway, just goes to show that sometimes the movie you think is perfectly engineered for a specific person doesn't always connect. i thought my mom's obsession with murder mysteries and her love for lamb imagery and the fact that this is basically The Land Before Time meets Knives Out would make this an instant classic to her but I was wrong.

it's so ridiculously good and i'm glad i finally saw it again. both this and Brand New Day have endings that make me happy.

Watched with Shelby

item.title: Midsommar, 2019 - ★★★★★ (contains spoilers)
item.description:
This review may contain spoilers.

The Rotvälta long take starts with Mark in tow with Josh, approaching Pelle in the garden. The camera only cuts to join Mark as Father Ulf is sprinting toward him, so we can catch up with him long after he has left the frame and the suspense is built. It’s truly something to watch. 

The juxtaposition of American and Swedish concepts of what is sacred and what is profane is something the film is interested in, and this ends up as the most comedic sequence of the entire runtime. I remember Ulf's hysteria made theater audiences laugh out loud.

The image looks like shit on HBO Max. Anytime there's darkness or black, it's all rectangles. Really wish there was something we could do about these awful, ass streaming services... like make the executives jump off a cliff. Or burn them in a custom teddy bear suit. Or turn them into a Yuletide tree. Or give them the Blood Eagle. Or just straight up hit them upside the head with a hammer.

item.title: The Odyssey, 2026 - ★★★★½
item.description:
"Benny Safdie was in this movie?"

— me, watching the end credits of Nolan's The Odyssey

I would never have guessed that Agamemnon was played by Benny fucking Safdie. It was pretty cool the way Nolan used the character to show Odysseus' discipline to war through the visual motif of the camera following Agamemnon into battle.

So many great performances but Robert Pattinson has the most fun. Charlize Theron, Anne Hathaway, Zendaya, Lupito N'yongo, and holy shit Samantha Morton — all of them enraptured me in the precious little screen time they steal from Matt Damon's glorious abs.

Only a few things stood out to me as leaving me wanting: the riddle of "Nobody" with Polyphemus was omitted; the sirens are depicted but we don't see any sailors who abandoned ship meet their end; the Scylla and Charybdis fight felt like something the movie was trying to get out of the way more than anything. And PENELOPE'S trick! COME ON! This is one of those times where I want another 15-20 minutes of runtime

ABSOLUTELY LOVED the score and the use of Travis Scott as a bard. I learned today by way of James Blake's social media that he had a part in the score and I told myself I'd recognize it and believe you me I knew it from the chord progression just before his velvety voice filled up the auditorium.

I was moved by this epic.

with Drake, Logan, Eric, Mary, and Jennie. Vinny took the photo.

My interpretation of these vibes led me to review my watchlist as well as my diary and I sought these qualities:
- Visual: muted/desaturated, bare trees, overcast skies, early darkness
- Emotional: contemplative melancholy, not depression exactly but... reckoning

item.title: JXNFC: Jake Sullivan’s Top 20
item.description:
• Cool Hand Luke

    A crash course in humanity. 

    "No man can eat 50 eggs."

  • The Godfather

    A crash course in film. Perfect in every aspect.

  • Blood Simple

    #3 is a revolving door of Coen films. This spot belongs to whichever I'm feeling the most on a given day. Their debut is underappreciated and seems like an appropriate placeholder.

  • Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid

    Every top 20 should have a western. And the best westerns are about bucking authority and beating the odds.

  • The Truman Show

    My life is definitely not filled by paid actors. But my brain thinks it might be.

  • Big Night

    The movie that taught me to appreciate food. And business. And Louie Prima.

    "Bite your teeth into the ass of life."

  • White Men Can't Jump

    Iconic 90s.

  • Thicker Than Water

    When I am wistful, surf docs settle my soul. This one is my go to.

  • Good Will Hunting

    Robin Williams at his very best and most vulnerable. RIP.

  • Attack the Block

    Pure fun. Easily my favorite monster movie.

item.title: JXNFC: Jonathan Miles’ Top 20 Films
item.description:
Classics, action, comedy, fantasy. This list has a little of everything.

  1. The Big Lebowski

    The greatest film ever made, bar none. Shut the fuck up, Donny

  2. The Nice Guys

    Just two guys, in way over their heads.

  3. There Will Be Blood

    One of the greatest Method acting performances of all time, although my contention will ever be that Daniel Day-Lewis deserved his second Oscar before this for Gangs of New York.

  4. Hell or High Water

    The best Texas noir film since No Country For Old Men.

  5. Pride & Prejudice

    A stirringly scored, beautifully shot adaptation of the Austen novel.

  6. The Searchers

    A visually brilliant, brutally spectacular film, and the performance that should have won John Wayne his Academy Award, for bitter, racist ex-Confederate Ethan Edwards.

  7. Zodiac

    David Fincher’s masterpiece. A stacked cast and a case that was never solved.

  8. When Harry Met Sally...

    The ultimate rom-com

  9. Talladega Nights: The Ballad of Ricky Bobby

    If you eat the DVD, it tastes like America

  10. Silver Linings Playbook

    Go Birds

item.title: JXNFC: Quentin Jones' Top 20
item.description:
Quentin Jones, friend of the film club, listed his top 20 on the most recent episode of Jackson Film Club The Podcast.

Quentin found himself in Jackson after working on the film crew for the episode of We Are Here created in Jackson in 2022. His first and foremost reason for his residence in the city is the love of his life, Lydia. His second reason is his mission for cannabis awareness and advancement in the state's new medical marijuana program. His third reason is the great dance floor at Shade.

This top 20 list features epic American classics and some of the most innovative and groundbreaking cinema in the world. Tune in to our conversation wherever you get your podcasts.

Though this is presented as a ranked list, the films in positions 22 - 24 are honorable mentions and despicable artists-now-canceled.

item.title: JXNFC - Animated Features
item.description:
This list was the basis of a special podcast episode. Check the link for more

https://jxnfilm.club/#animated-features

  • The Land Before Time

    Entered by Michael

    This film is my waypoint for consciousness -- I came to an understanding of death emotionally because of this movie. Nothing has ever quite hit the same, to be honest.

  • Rock-A-Doodle

    Entered by Michael

    When my parents would go to their weekly bowling league, I was the kid who would change the TV to Rock-A-Doodle at the childcare center next door.

  • One Hundred and One Dalmatians

    Entered by Michael

  • Princess Mononoke

    Entered by Michael

    This was when I realized that animation is for grownups, and that grownup stories can be told through animation. I love how this changed my imagination.

  • Spirited Away

    Entered by Michael

    I found this not far from the age of Chihiro. It means a lot to me because I moved twice before the age of 10 and this film teaches about life in its own way, through the eyes of a young person who has been Spirited Away.

  • Samurai Champloo

    Entered by Michael

    This anime popped up on Adult Swim, but I never finished the series on the air. Nearly 20 years later, I've finally watched the entirety and absolutely loved the ending.

  • The Hobbit

    Entered by Morgan

item.title: 2022 Goal: 100 New Directors
item.description:
I started the year with a pretty interesting ratio of 1.28:1 for number of films by a director. On 14 October 2021 I reached a milestone of 500 directors from 646 logged films, spanning 41 countries, inspiring my 2022 goal of watching 100 movies introducing myself to that many more new directors. As of completion of this goal, my ratio is 1.33 movies per director with over 700 directors logged. I look forward to seeing where it's at when I hit 1500 movies logged

tl;dr: for every movie on this list, 2022 is the first time I’ve seen something from that director.

  1. The Hand of God
  2. The Lost Daughter
  3. Summer of Soul (...Or, When the Revolution Could Not Be Televised)
  4. The Mask of Zorro
  5. The Paradise Next Door
  6. Lunch on the Grass
  7. Doctor Strange
  8. The Good, the Bad and the Ugly
